newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks stage biggest rally ever to record close.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks stage biggest rally ever to record close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks staged their biggest point gain in history on Friday, forging into record ground on a wave of handover euphoria to close at an all-time high.
The blue chip Hang Seng Index closed on a massive gain of 647.87 points, or 4.47 percent, at 15,154.36.
Turnover was a record at HK$26.6 billion.
"What we are seeing here is definitely handover euphoria coming through here today," said Jake van der Kamp, investment strategist at HG Asia.

Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule in 11 days after 156 years of colonial rule. As well as boosting sentiment in the local stock market, the territory's change in sovereignty has revived talk that a mainland company could buy a stake in Hang Seng Bank Ltd, prompting a surge in its shares.
"The main engine for this surge is the banking sector and the rumour that China will buy a stake in Hang Seng Bank," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
Shares in Hang Seng Bank jumped above HK$100 for the first time ever on Friday, climbing HK$12.75 to HK$109.50 after hitting a record high of HK$110.00 during the session.
Shares in its parent HSBC Holdings Plc advanced HK$7.00 to HK$233.00. Turnover in the two stocks totalled HK$3.13 billion.
Overall turnover beat the previous market record of HK$26.48 billion hit on June 2 this year.
"Turnover in the last few weeks has mainly come from red chips but today we have seen the blue chips come back," said Tam. He said the Hang Seng Index could push higher next week.
"Fair value is around 15,000 and generally I think it will stay above 15,000 going through to the handover," said van der Kamp.
HSI Services Ltd, the compiler of the Hang Seng Index, said Friday's 647.87 point gain beat the previous record of 597.74 points registered on January 14, 1994.
Also driving the surge in prices was the property sector, with investors hoping that expected government measures to curb rising property prices would not damage the real estate market.
Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd rose HK$3.50 to HK$78.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd gained HK$5.25 to HK$95.25.

Shares in Furama Hotel Enterprises Ltd soared HK$6.00 to HK$32.00 after Lai Sun Development Co Ltd said it would buy a 45.42 percent stake in the company and make a general offer at HK$33.50 per share. Lai Sun Development rose HK$0.45 to HK$8.95.
